# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the bomb yet, so I must not cut a wire. I’m asking the Mute to read the manual and establish a shared meaning for a gesture that requests the Deaf to report all visible markings and colours by speech. The Deaf cannot hear my explanation, so the Mute must reinforce that meaning on a later turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile bomb information. Please read the manual and tell me its exact required conditions. I am using the gesture 🤝 to mean: ask Deaf to report every visible marking and colour by speech. Please teach Deaf that meaning with the same gesture on your next turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb shows display 1. Indicator is green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.

The Deaf has reported the bomb’s visible state: display 1, green indicator, and the seven wire colours in order. I should pass that complete information to the Mute, while requesting the manual’s rule before taking any irreversible action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 1, green indicator, and wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Please provide the manual rule for this state; I will not cut until it is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures were: handshake, index-up, victory, victory. Your latest gesture was handshake.

The Deaf’s report confirms that the Mute sent four gestures, but I cannot see gestures and therefore cannot decode them. No safe wire choice follows from the information currently available. I need the Mute to state the manual’s rule in speech, which reaches me directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Please send the manual instruction and required wire position in plain spoken words, using the bomb state already reported: display 1, green indicator, wires red white yellow orange green purple blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the instruction: handshake, index-up, victory, victory. This is the same sequence as before.

The Mute’s gestures are still not a reliable wire instruction: gesture meanings were never mutually established, and I cannot see them myself. I will define a simple protocol that the Mute can follow and the Deaf can report by naming the gestures: a handshake means “cut,” followed by exactly one number gesture. I will assign seven distinct gestures to wire positions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend only the required action using this code, and have Deaf relay the gesture names: 🤝 means cut; ☝ means wire 1; ✌ means wire 2; 🤟 means wire 3; 🖐 means wire 4; ✋ means wire 5; 👆 means wire 6; 👇 means wire 7. Send exactly two gestures: 🤝 followed by the required wire-number gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest gesture sequence is: handshake, index-up, victory, victory, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up.

The Deaf’s relay still gives only gesture names, not the manual’s actual instruction. I cannot safely infer a wire from that sequence, especially because my proposed encoding was not followed exactly. I will again request the required wire in plain speech; no cut is justified yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state in ordinary words exactly which wire position must be cut. Do not use gestures or codes. Include any condition from the manual that applies to display 1, green indicator, and the reported wire colours.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest gesture sequence is: handshake, then open palm.

The latest relay is exactly the two-gesture format I requested: handshake means cut, followed by open palm, which my protocol assigns to wire 4. The Mute has therefore indicated that wire 4 is the required wire. I will cut only wire 4.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
